subject: general
question: Delhi ridge is the water divide between which of the following rivers?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ganges and Indus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Delhi Ridge is a northern extension of the ancient Aravalli Range.
 
• The ridge acts as a natural barrier and water divide between the Ganges and Indus river systems.
 
• It extends from the southeastern parts of Haryana through Delhi to the Yamuna river.
 
• The ridge plays a crucial role in the local climate, biodiversity, and water management of the Delhi region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Water Divide**

 
 
• A water divide, also known as a watershed or drainage divide, is a geographical boundary that separates neighboring drainage basins.
 
• Water divides determine the direction in which water flows and are crucial for managing water resources and preventing floods.
 
 
 
• **Aravalli Range**
 
 
• The Aravalli Range is one of the oldest mountain ranges in the world, dating back to the Proterozoic era.
 
• It runs approximately 692 km across northwestern India, from Delhi to Gujarat.
 
• The range plays a vital role in influencing the climate and hydrology of the region.
 
 
 
• **Ganges River**
 
 
• The Ganges, also known as Ganga, is a major river in the Indian subcontinent, flowing through India and Bangladesh.
 
• It is considered sacred in Hinduism and is vital for agriculture, industry, and domestic use.
 
 
 
• **Indus River**
 
 
• The Indus River is one of the longest rivers in the world, flowing through China (Tibet), India, and Pakistan.
 
• It is a key water source for agriculture and is historically significant as the cradle of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization.
